name: North Dakota
source: North Dakota reader session (Stage 5 tools), 2026-11-19: the November 2026 Open States dump converted with scripts/stage5/openstates/; every floor roll call of an 89-bill dry batch (171 roll calls, 2017-2025) read from the daily journals on ndlegis.gov with the verifier's own fetch, and each member's vote compared with the dump where the dump holds one. Three bill texts were read for their marks (2017 HB 1279 as passed and a proposed amendment; 2025 HB 1326 as introduced, also as a page image); no text was measured in bulk.
sessions: The Legislative Assembly meets in regular session once every two years, in odd years, from January to late April: the 65th in 2017, the 66th in 2019, the 67th in 2021, the 68th in 2023, the 69th in 2025. Open States names the regular sessions "65" to "69". Bill numbers start again each Assembly: House bills HB 1001 up, Senate bills SB 2001 up, concurrent resolutions HCR 3001 and SCR 4001 up, and other resolution series. Special sessions sit under /special-session/ or /special-2/ on the site (67S1 in November 2021; and two special sessions of the 69th in January and September 2026, which the dump files inside the 69th's folder as votes "not placed") and are not read by the tools. House 94 seats, Senate 47; two representatives and one senator per district.
bill_data: No LegiScan dataset is on disk for North Dakota. Bills, sponsors and roll calls come from Open States data, converted to the same folder layout (ND-900119 to ND-900124: the regular sessions 65 to 69 and the 2021 special session 67S1; scripts/stage5/openstates/README.md). Each folder carries a .openstates.json; its ids are ours and no legiscan.com page exists for them.

The dump holds no roll call at all for the 66th and 67th Assemblies (2019, 2021), and its votes name members by family name only ("Becker, Rick C.", "Lee, J."). So no North Dakota dump vote is placed: scripts/stage5/openstates/fetch-legislature-rollcalls.ts reads each bill's action page (/assembly/<NN-YYYY>/regular/bill-actions/ba<num>.html), keeps each "Second reading, passed|failed to pass|adopted ..., yeas N nays M" row, and reads that vote from the day's journal page the row links to; convert.py places only those (record_is_the_floor) and keeps every other dump vote marked committee, with the reason in _openstates.not_placed. Run the fetch for every bill the scan finds, session by session (65 to 69), then convert the whole state again.

Compared 2026-11-19: 171 floor roll calls read from the record, 0 refused. 78 (2019 and 2021) have no dump copy because the dump has none for those years. Of the other 93, 4 were settled by the tally among several on one day and 3 sat a day later in the dump than in the journal; 0 are on the record only. Tally differences: 0. Member votes compared: 6,871, differences: 0. 30 member votes are unreadable for two labels: "Christensen" (2023 House, 19 votes) and "Brown" (2025 House, 11 votes), each printed bare while the Assembly's member list shows two members it fits; the dump names them Cole Christensen and Collette Brown and agrees with the record's vote on all 30.

The journal prints family names ("Anderson, B.", "Becker, Rick C.", "Roers Jones", "Speaker Bellew"), so the reader takes the Assembly's member list (/assembly/<NN-YYYY>/regular/members/members-by-district) as a second document and maps each label to the one full name it fits; a label two members fit gives no line. convert.py links the record's full names to Open States people (ms_full_names). Roster legislators: 141, all linked, and each link checked against the 69th Assembly's member list through the member's biography address (/biography/collette-brown), which the site keeps across Assemblies. One person (Daniel Johnston) needed a second idmap line by hand, because the datasets hold him under two ids ("Daniel Johnston" 2017-2020, "Dan Johnston" 2025). The datasets also hold each 2023 and 2025 member a second time under the title ("Representative Adam Goldwyn"); those people carry only dump votes that are not placed, and need no line. Four sitting representatives (Adam Goldwyn, Dave Rustebakke, Dustin McNally, Jamie Selzler) took their seats after the 2025 regular session; their only votes are in the 2026 special sessions, which are not read, so they have no vote finding.

votes.floor_rule: A vote is cited as the daily journal page that prints it, with the bill after a #: ndlegis.gov/assembly/<NN-YYYY>/regular/journals/<hr|sr>-dailyjnl-<day>.pdf#Page<page>-<HB1326> (#Page820-HB1326). The page tells apart two votes on one bill on one day (2025 HB 1326 failed on page 811 and passed on page 820). The journal prints the bill's heading ("HB 1326: A BILL for an Act ..."), "ROLL CALL", the question with its tally ("... there were 56 YEAS, 35 NAYS, 2 ABSENT OR EXCUSED AND NOT VOTING"; 2017-2023 print EXCUSED and ABSENT AND NOT VOTING apart), the YEAS, NAYS and absent groups as family names separated by semicolons, and the result ("HB 1326 passed."). The reader (src/lib/stateRollCallEvidence.ts) reads the Assembly's member list as a second document to turn each label into a full name, and reads a vote only when the question is final passage of the bill or final adoption of a resolution, each group lists the count the question prints for its heading, the running heads give the address's day, chamber and page, the result line names the bill, and every label fits one member. A member who did not vote is written as absent or excused, never as a Yea or a Nay. Committee votes, the adoption of a division or of amendments, motions to reconsider and every other motion are not mapped.
gaps: Committee votes, votes adopting a division of a bill or amendments, and every other motion are not votes on the bill and are not mapped (runner, 2026-11-16). A bill voted in divisions (2025 HB 1588: Division A and Division B, then the bill) keeps only the vote on the whole bill.

A printed label that fits no member of that Assembly's list, or more than one, gives no line. The member list shows everyone who sat during the Assembly, replacements included, with no dates: in the dry batch this hit "Christensen" (2023 House, 19 votes: Cole Christensen and Rose Christensen, who later held his District 24 seat) and "Brown" (2025 House, 11 votes: Collette Brown and TJ Brown). Collette Brown, who sits now, gets no line on those 11 votes.
A resolution adopted on a voice vote ("Second reading, adopted" with no tally) has no roll call. Special sessions are not read.

texts.marks: Read on 3 texts (2017 HB 1279 as passed and a proposed amendment, 2025 HB 1326 as introduced; 2026-11-19). In a bill that amends existing law, words added are UNDERLINED and words deleted are STRUCK THROUGH (a line through the middle), as the page image of 2025 HB 1326 shows. Plain pdftotext keeps neither mark and runs the struck word into the added one with no space ("A personAn individual", "himselfoneself", "suchthe other personindividual"), so a text read as plain words says both the old and the new law at once. Read the page as an image before quoting any passage inside an amending section. A proposed amendment (the ...a.pdf and ...m.pdf files) is written as instructions ("Page 1, line 1, after ... replace ... with ..."), not as the bill.
texts.note: A bill's documents are /assembly/<NN-YYYY>/regular/documents/<YY-NNNN-NNNNN>.pdf; the last five digits number the version (01000 introduced, 02000 and up amended or engrossed; a suffix a or m marks an amendment file). The dump links 2017 and 2019 texts and bill pages on the old host www.legis.nd.gov without /regular/; the texts still redirect there, the bill pages answer 404. convert.py writes the current address for both (nd_links): the bill's overview page /regular/bill-overview/bo<num>.html, and /regular/documents/ for texts. A special session's addresses (/special-session/) answer 404 on the current host: they are kept and counted (nd_link_not_rewritten).

search_note: North Dakota sponsorships and House and Senate floor votes for 2017 to 2025 come from the bill data on disk, checked against the legislature's own journals: skip the legislature's bill pages and journals, and add the place "sponsor list: covered by bulk bill data". Spend the search on their own words (statements, campaign pages, newsletters, floor remarks, interviews, questionnaires). If any page returns 403, 429, an empty page or a bot check, record it as blocked and move on: do not retry it with a different user agent, headers or tool.
bill_table_note:
- North Dakota's Assembly meets every two years, in odd years; bill numbers start again each Assembly (HB 1001, SB 2001).
- Floor votes kept: final passage of a bill and final adoption of a resolution. Committee votes, votes on a division of a bill or on amendments, and other motions are not floor votes on the bill.
- Texts: UNDERLINED words are added to existing law; STRUCK-THROUGH words are deleted. Plain text keeps neither mark and runs the old word into the new one ("A personAn individual"): check the page image before quoting an amended passage.
quirks: robots.txt (Drupal's default) disallows nothing under /assembly/ and states no crawl delay. The reader waits one second between requests. No 403, 429 or bot check was met on 2026-11-19.

One vote needs the day's journal PDF (about 200-250 KB) and the Assembly's member list (about 250 KB). The line tool took 1 minute 22 seconds for 200 random votes from an empty page cache (70 journals).

A bill's action page dates a vote by when it was entered, which can be a day off the journal's own date; the journal's running head is the vote's date, and the dump agrees with the journal except for three 2023-2025 votes it files a day later.

The journal's first line on most pages is a bare "Page N" followed by the running head; some pages (a day's last) lack it. The running heads alternate: odd pages "35th DAY WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 22, 2017 787", even pages "788 JOURNAL OF THE HOUSE 35th DAY". A name can break over a line with no semicolon ("Roers" / "Jones", "Speaker" / "Bellew").

The member list shows everyone who sat during the Assembly, replacements included, as tiles with no dates. A replacement who shares a family name with another member makes that family name unreadable for the whole Assembly.

The dump holds every 2023 and 2025 member a second time as a name-only person named with the title ("Representative Adam Goldwyn"), carrying only unplaced votes. link_check.py does not offer these; they need no idmap line.

The saved text of a bill prints each margin line number (1 to 31) on its own line inside the law text, and a section label ("Section 1.") opens each section; a quote copied across two sections or two separate passages reads as one passage that is not in the bill (2026-11-19, 72 texts of 2017-2025).
